**R1** (RC0402FR-073K4L — 3400)

3400Ω, nearest E96 (1%) value to the 3386.3Ω ideal. With C1=47nF it gives f_c = 1/(2π·R·C) = 996.0 Hz against the 1000 Hz asked for. 47nF ceramic, rated 16V against a 5V supply. Chosen first because it puts R1 inside 1000–100000Ω. A 10% part, so it dominates the cutoff tolerance — the ±1% resistor contributes roughly a tenth as much spread.

## What it will do

- **cutoff_hz**: 995.963 Hz nominal, and between 896.457 Hz and 1.1178 kHz across the full component tolerance — a spread of ±12.2%.

- **resistance_ohm**: 3.4 kΩ nominal, and between 3.366 kΩ and 3.434 kΩ across the full component tolerance — a spread of ±1.0%.

- **capacitance_f**: 47 nF nominal, and between 42.3 nF and 51.7 nF across the full component tolerance — a spread of ±10.0%.

- **vout_at_cutoff_v**: 3.53553 V

- **attenuation_at_cutoff_db**: -3.0103 dB

These are closed-form results over the whole tolerance box, not a single simulated point, computed by monotone corners.

## What you asked for

Indicator LED on D13 at 10 mA

- **led_current_ma**: 10
- mcu: arduino_uno

## Why each component

**U1** (ATmega328P-PU)

Arduino Uno MCU driving the LED from D13. Each GPIO is rated 20 mA recommended, 40 mA absolute; this design stays at or under 11.7 mA over every part tolerance.

**LED1** (150080RS75000)

Red LED, V_f 1.96 V at 9.95 mA on its fitted diode model (datasheet 1.7–2.4 V at 20 mA). A lower-V_f part in the same spread raises the current to 11.7 mA — still under its 30 mA rating.

**R1** (RC0402FR-07280RL — 280)

280Ω, the E96 value nearest 10 mA. It sets I = (V_pin − V_f)/R1 ≈ 9.95 mA; halving it would roughly double the current and, past 20 mA, overload the pin.

**C1** (CL05B104KO5NNNC — 100nF)

100nF X7R bypass on U1's supply pin, placed close to it. It supplies the fast edges the rail's trace inductance cannot; without it switching noise couples into every line on the board. Rated 16 V against the 5 V rail.

## What it will do

- **led_current_ma**: 9.9544 mA nominal, and between 8.19745 mA and 11.7303 mA across the full component tolerance — a spread of ±17.8%.

- **gpio_current_ma**: 9.9544 mA nominal, and between 8.19745 mA and 11.7303 mA across the full component tolerance — a spread of ±17.8%.

- **led_forward_v**: 1.96391 V

- **pin_voltage_v**: 4.75114 V

- **r1_power_mw**: 27.7452 mW nominal, and between 19.0037 mW and 38.1429 mW across the full component tolerance — a spread of ±37.5%.

- **supply_current_ma**: 59.9544 mA nominal, and between 58.1975 mA and 61.7303 mA across the full component tolerance — a spread of ±3.0%.

These are closed-form results over the whole tolerance box, not a single simulated point, computed by monotone corners.

## Validation

Every structural rule passed. That does not mean the design is correct — it means nothing it checks for is wrong.

## What breaks if you change it

- The **r1_power_mw** tolerance dominates the result at ±37.5%. Tightening anything else would barely move the outcome; if you need a narrower band, that is the part to change.

- **U1** has only 0.5 V of margin over the 5 V rail. Raising the supply would exceed its 5.5 V rating.

- **R1** is rated 50 V on a 5 V rail, so it has margin; it would only become a risk if you raised the supply above 50 V.

- **C1** is rated 16 V on a 5 V rail, so it has margin; it would only become a risk if you raised the supply above 16 V.

## What this does not tell you

- These numbers hold under the **mna_ideal+mcu_pin_thevenin+shockley_diode** model, over tolerance box, at steady state, for a single stimulus. Outside that they say nothing.

- The model is mathematics, not hardware. It cannot see parasitic inductance, board capacitance, contact resistance, or a part behaving outside its datasheet — any of those would shift the real result away from the numbers above.

- Thermal behaviour, EMI, and manufacturing yield are not assessed at all.

## What you asked for

Modbus RTU master on RS-485 at 9600 baud, 1 slave(s)

- mcu: arduino_uno

## Why each component

**U1** (ATmega328P-PU)

Arduino Uno MCU as Modbus RTU master: SoftwareSerial TX on D11, RX on D10, direction on D2. Hardware Serial (D0/D1) stays free for uploads and debugging.

**U2** (MAX485ECSA)

MAX485 half-duplex transceiver, DE and RE tied to D2: high transmits, low listens. Its supply window is 4.75–5.25 V; a 3.3 V design needs the MAX3485 instead.

**R1** (RC1206FR-07120RL — 120)

120Ω termination across A/B, matching the cable's 120 Ω impedance so edges do not reflect. 1206, not 0402: a driver can put 5 V across it (208 mW), over three times an 0402's rating.

**R2** (RC0402FR-07549RL — 549)

549Ω fail-safe bias, A to VCC: the largest E96 value keeping idle V_AB ≥ 250 mV over tolerance with a far-end terminator. Idle V_AB is 259 mV nominal, 254 mV worst case; a larger value would let the idle bus sag toward the 200 mV threshold, where receivers read noise.

**R3** (RC0402FR-07549RL — 549)

549Ω fail-safe bias, B to GND: the largest E96 value keeping idle V_AB ≥ 250 mV over tolerance with a far-end terminator. Idle V_AB is 259 mV nominal, 254 mV worst case; a larger value would let the idle bus sag toward the 200 mV threshold, where receivers read noise.

**R4** (RC0402FR-0710KL — 10000)

10000Ω pull-down on DE/RE. While the MCU is in reset, and until the firmware sets it, D2 is high-impedance, and a floating DE can switch the driver on and put noise on a bus other nodes are using. This holds the transceiver in receive mode: DE/RE stays at or below 50 mV against the pin's leakage, under the 0.8 V the transceiver reads as low. It draws current only while the pin drives DE high to transmit.

**C1** (CL05B104KO5NNNC — 100nF)

100nF X7R bypass on U2's supply pin, placed close to it. It supplies the fast edges the rail's trace inductance cannot; without it switching noise couples into every line on the board. Rated 16 V against the 5 V rail.

## What it will do

- **v_ab_idle_mv**: 259.067 mV nominal, and between 254.198 mV and 264.025 mV across the full component tolerance — a spread of ±1.9%.

- **bus_load_ohm**: 56.8912 Ω nominal, and between 56.3223 Ω and 57.4601 Ω across the full component tolerance — a spread of ±1.0%.

- **termination_power_mw**: 210.438 mW nominal, and between 0 mW and 210.438 mW across the full component tolerance — a spread of ±100.0%.

- **supply_current_ma**: 54.6035 mA

- **de_idle_mv**: 50.5 mV nominal, and between 0 mV and 50.5 mV across the full component tolerance — a spread of ±100.0%.

These are closed-form results over the whole tolerance box, not a single simulated point, computed by monotone corners.

## Validation

Every structural rule passed. That does not mean the design is correct — it means nothing it checks for is wrong.

## What breaks if you change it

- The **termination_power_mw** tolerance dominates the result at ±100.0%. Tightening anything else would barely move the outcome; if you need a narrower band, that is the part to change.

- **U1** has only 0.5 V of margin over the 5 V rail. Raising the supply would exceed its 5.5 V rating.

- **U2** has only 0.25 V of margin over the 5 V rail. Raising the supply would exceed its 5.25 V rating.

- **R1** is rated 200 V on a 5 V rail, so it has margin; it would only become a risk if you raised the supply above 200 V.

- **R2** is rated 50 V on a 5 V rail, so it has margin; it would only become a risk if you raised the supply above 50 V.

- **R3** is rated 50 V on a 5 V rail, so it has margin; it would only become a risk if you raised the supply above 50 V.

- **R4** is rated 50 V on a 5 V rail, so it has margin; it would only become a risk if you raised the supply above 50 V.

- **C1** is rated 16 V on a 5 V rail, so it has margin; it would only become a risk if you raised the supply above 16 V.

## What this does not tell you

- These numbers hold under the **mna_ideal+mcu_as_100R** model, over tolerance box, at steady state, for a single stimulus. Outside that they say nothing.

- The model is mathematics, not hardware. It cannot see parasitic inductance, board capacitance, contact resistance, or a part behaving outside its datasheet — any of those would shift the real result away from the numbers above.

- Thermal behaviour, EMI, and manufacturing yield are not assessed at all.

generate.explanation:
## What you asked for

Room monitor: an Uno reads a DHT22, sounds a buzzer above 30 °C, and lights a status LED

- mcu: arduino_uno

## Why each component

**U1** (ATmega328P-PU)

Arduino Uno R3 MCU shared by 3 blocks — climate: Arduino Uno MCU reading the DHT22 on D2. The pin is bidirectional: it pulls DATA low for the start pulse, then listens.; alarm: Arduino Uno MCU switching the load from D8. The pin sources at most 3.66 mA into Q1's base over every part tolerance, under the 20 mA recommended per pin.; status: Arduino Uno MCU driving the LED from D13. Each GPIO is rated 20 mA recommended, 40 mA absolute; this design stays at or under 11.7 mA over every part tolerance.

**U2** (DHT22)

DHT22: ±0.5 °C, ±2 %RH over a single-wire open-drain bus. It cannot be read faster than every 2 s, and without R1 its DATA line never goes high.

**R1** (RC0402FR-0710KL — 10000)

10000Ω, the Aosong datasheet value, fast enough for 0.3 m of cable. Rise time ≈ 1.1 µs worst case; halving R1 halves it but doubles the 0.5 mA sunk while DATA is held low.

**C1** (CL05B104KO5NNNC — 100nF)

100nF bypass across the shared rail at the MCU's supply pin, one for the board: every block's generator places one, and on one board they are the same part. Without it switching noise couples into every line on the board.

**Q1** (MMBT2222ALT1G)

NPN low-side switch for the 30 mA load. It needs 3 mA of base current (I_C/10) to saturate at V_CE ≤ 0.3 V; it gets at least 3.04 mA. Under-driven, it would sit in its linear region and heat.

**R2** (RC0402FR-071K21L — 1210)

1210Ω, the largest E96 value that still saturates Q1 at the worst corner. Base current 3.04–3.66 mA; a larger R1 starves the base, a smaller one loads the pin for nothing.

**J1** (22-27-2021 — 166.667)

Header for the load: pin 1 to the 5 V rail, pin 2 to Q1's collector. The value is the load's equivalent resistance as declared — 5 V at 30 mA — which is what the netlist models; it is not a part on the board.

Confidence on this choice is 85%. Check it against your own requirements before ordering — a wrong part here would not be caught by simulation, because simulation models the value, not the part.

**D1** (1N4148W-7-F)

Flyback diode across the load. When Q1 turns off, the load's inductance drives its 30 mA on through D1 instead of spiking Q1's collector past its 40 V rating.

**LED1** (150080RS75000)

Red LED, V_f 1.96 V at 9.95 mA on its fitted diode model (datasheet 1.7–2.4 V at 20 mA). A lower-V_f part in the same spread raises the current to 11.7 mA — still under its 30 mA rating.

**R3** (RC0402FR-07280RL — 280)

280Ω, the E96 value nearest 10 mA. It sets I = (V_pin − V_f)/R1 ≈ 9.95 mA; halving it would roughly double the current and, past 20 mA, overload the pin.

## Validation

Every structural rule passed. That does not mean the design is correct — it means nothing it checks for is wrong.

## What breaks if you change it

- **U1** has only 0.5 V of margin over the 5 V rail. Raising the supply would exceed its 5.5 V rating.

- **U2** has only 0.5 V of margin over the 5 V rail. Raising the supply would exceed its 5.5 V rating.

- **R1** is rated 50 V on a 5 V rail, so it has margin; it would only become a risk if you raised the supply above 50 V.

- **C1** is rated 16 V on a 5 V rail, so it has margin; it would only become a risk if you raised the supply above 16 V.

- **Q1** is rated 40 V on a 5 V rail, so it has margin; it would only become a risk if you raised the supply above 40 V.

- **R2** is rated 50 V on a 5 V rail, so it has margin; it would only become a risk if you raised the supply above 50 V.

- **D1** is rated 100 V on a 5 V rail, so it has margin; it would only become a risk if you raised the supply above 100 V.

- **R3** is rated 50 V on a 5 V rail, so it has margin; it would only become a risk if you raised the supply above 50 V.

## What this does not tell you

- Thermal behaviour, EMI, and manufacturing yield are not assessed at all.

rows.justification: 10000Ω, the Aosong datasheet value, fast enough for 0.3 m of cable. Rise time ≈ 1.1 µs worst case; halving R1 halves it but doubles the 0.5 mA sunk while DATA is held low.

rows.justification: 100nF bypass across the shared rail at the MCU's supply pin, one for the board: every block's generator places one, and on one board they are the same part. Without it switching noise couples into every line on the board.
NPN low-side switch for the 30 mA load. It needs 3 mA of base current (I_C/10) to saturate at V_CE ≤ 0.3 V; it gets at least 3.04 mA. Under-driven, it would sit in its linear region and heat.
1210Ω, the largest E96 value that still saturates Q1 at the worst corner. Base current 3.04–3.66 mA; a larger R1 starves the base, a smaller one loads the pin for nothing.

Header for the load: pin 1 to the 5 V rail, pin 2 to Q1's collector. The value is the load's equivalent resistance as declared — 5 V at 30 mA — which is what the netlist models; it is not a part on the board.
Flyback diode across the load. When Q1 turns off, the load's inductance drives its 30 mA on through D1 instead of spiking Q1's collector past its 40 V rating.
Red LED, V_f 1.96 V at 9.95 mA on its fitted diode model (datasheet 1.7–2.4 V at 20 mA). A lower-V_f part in the same spread raises the current to 11.7 mA — still under its 30 mA rating.
280Ω, the E96 value nearest 10 mA. It sets I = (V_pin − V_f)/R1 ≈ 9.95 mA; halving it would roughly double the current and, past 20 mA, overload the pin.
